title: moolut.github.io — Retro CRT Portfolio
problem: Generic portfolio templates feel identical and forgettable.
result: A cohesive retro CRT portfolio with modular pages and a scalable Case Files viewer.
overview: A retro CRT-themed portfolio built as a modular site with reusable UI components and interactive pages. The goal was to create a memorable interface that supports quick scanning and deep dives.
whatIBuilt: A cohesive CRT UI system (scanlines/noise, typography, consistent components).
Multiple themed pages (index/whoami/achievements/projects) with shared design language.
A Case Files project viewer with filters and modal-based case reading.
techDetails: Frontend stack: Astro + Svelte + TypeScript + CSS.
Component-first structure (cards, tabs, modal viewer, artifacts dock).
UI states designed for both hover and keyboard focus navigation.
outputs: A production-ready portfolio with a distinctive theme and structured project presentation.

title: pov_fan — POV Fan Firmware + Control Software
problem: Render dynamic visuals on a high-speed POV fan reliably and synchronously.
result: A synchronized LED rendering pipeline for stable image/text output on custom POV fan hardware.
overview: Firmware and control software for a holographic POV (Persistence of Vision) fan display. The system renders images/text by synchronizing LED patterns with high-speed rotation timing to create a stable floating display illusion.
whatIBuilt: A timing-synchronized LED frame generation and playback pipeline.
Control logic to map image/text content into rotation-aligned LED frames.
A project structure suitable for firmware iteration and testing.
techDetails: Emphasis on stable timing: rotation alignment → frame scheduling → consistent output.
Firmware-oriented development with reproducible build/run workflow.
Implementation primarily in C++ with embedded tooling.
outputs: A repeatable approach to stable mid-air POV rendering on custom hardware.

title: smartcard-lab — ISO 7816 Communication + Security Experiments
problem: Implement smartcard communication flows and explore security considerations in practice.
result: Working ISO 7816 communication plus documented security experiments and countermeasure evaluation.
overview: SmartCard Security Project for TUM SmartCard Lab. Focused on implementing secure communication flows and evaluating security weaknesses and countermeasures with evidence-driven measurements.
whatIBuilt: ISO 7816 communication work and lab protocol tasks.
Countermeasure experiments targeting side-channel resistance.
Documentation/report artifacts capturing measurements and conclusions.
techDetails: Masking and shuffling countermeasures applied to AES S-box operations.
Power trace uniformity measurement before/after protections.
Performance vs security tradeoff evaluation and reporting.
outputs: Evidence-backed evaluation of countermeasures and their overhead.

title: embedded-systems-and-security — Course Lab Collection
problem: Need structured hands-on practice across embedded systems topics in one place.
result: A consolidated set of graded labs covering timing, exploitation, crypto, and HID side-channel concepts.
overview: Three graded assignments from TUM's Embedded Systems and Security course, each focusing on a different embedded reliability/security concept using the Infineon XMC4500 platform.
whatIBuilt: Assignment 1: LED Morse transmission + timing features driven by timers/interrupts.
Assignment 2: Stack overflow exploration + transition to authenticated encryption for secure command sending.
Assignment 3: USB HID keyboard emulation + timing side-channel exploitation workflow.
techDetails: Embedded timing + interrupt-driven interaction (timers, SysTick/CCU4-style workflows).
Practical memory exploitation lessons and mitigation considerations.
Secure messaging using authenticated encryption (libsodium-style secretbox approach).
USB HID protocol + keyboard layout handling + timing analysis.
outputs: A structured lab archive demonstrating embedded implementation and security analysis skills.

title: iot-security-ctf — CTF Solutions & Writeups
problem: Solve practical security challenges and keep solutions reproducible for later reference.
result: A structured writeup archive covering crypto, IoT protocol issues, and web vulnerabilities.
overview: Solutions and writeups for TUM IoT Security CTF challenges. Organized as a reusable archive with reasoning, steps, and artifacts where applicable.
whatIBuilt: Per-challenge solution notes and reproducible steps.
Exploit/analysis code when useful to support the writeups.
A structured repo layout for quick lookup and revision.
techDetails: Cryptography/cryptanalysis coverage (including classical cipher work).
IoT protocol weaknesses and device exploitation themes.
Web security topics (injection/auth/session-style weaknesses).
outputs: A repeatable reference archive of solved challenges and security reasoning.

title: flappy-bird — ARM Cortex-M0 Assembly Game
problem: Build a complete game loop on constrained hardware using low-level code.
result: A working Flappy Bird clone demonstrating timing, input, rendering, and collision logic in ARM assembly.
overview: A Flappy Bird clone written entirely in ARM Cortex-M0 assembly to explore bare-metal programming and register-level rendering on constrained hardware.
whatIBuilt: A full game loop with timing and state management.
Interrupt-driven button input for game control.
Manual sprite/map rendering and collision detection.
techDetails: Low-level ARM instruction usage with manual register/memory management.
Stack operations and interrupt handling patterns.
Constraints-aware design for embedded execution.
outputs: A complete embedded game demonstrating low-level control and reliability under constraints.

title: Logic-Simulator — C++ / SFML Circuit Simulator
problem: Interactively simulate logic circuits with a visual interface.
result: A graphical sandbox to build and simulate logic gate networks and circuit behavior.
overview: A graphical logic circuit simulator built in C++ using SFML. Users can create circuits interactively and observe their behavior in real time.
whatIBuilt: A GUI for constructing circuits with draggable components.
A simulation engine for common digital components.
A sprite-based representation of logic elements and connections.
techDetails: Supported elements include AND/OR/XOR/NOT gates, D flip-flops, clock, LEDs.
OOP-driven design to model components and connections cleanly.
SFML-based rendering loop and interaction handling.
outputs: An interactive sandbox for experimenting with digital logic composition.
